transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I’ve started doing things that honestly scare me. Like, I’ll walk out in the middle of work deployments, or I’ll drive around late at night with no plan. That’s just not how I normally handle stress, and it’s worrying me.
Do you feel anxious before or while doing these things that scare you?

Yes. I feel keyed up when it’s happening, like I need to get away from whatever is in front of me. That’s when I’ll do things like leave in the middle of a deployment or just get in the car late at night with no real plan. It scares me because that’s not like me.
Do you usually avoid certain situations or activities because they make you feel anxious or uncomfortable?

Yes. I do. I’ll take the long way around the building just so I don’t have to pass certain areas. I avoid that floor whenever I can. And if people start talking about the contractor or the cutover, I usually shut the conversation down or find a reason to leave.
Do you often feel like you're inadequate or incompetent in social or professional situations?

I’m not sure I’d put it that way. I don’t usually think of myself as incompetent, especially at work. I might second-guess myself sometimes, but it’s not really a constant feeling of being inadequate socially or professionally.
Do you have recurring thoughts or ideas that you can't seem to get out of your head?

Yes. They’ll just come out of nowhere. If I’m in that conference area, or if someone raises their voice on a call, I suddenly get these images and sounds from that night in my head. It’s strong enough that I’ll lose track of what I was saying for a moment.
Do you ever feel like you're reliving that night, as if it's happening all over again?

Yes. Not all the time, but it happens. I’ll be in that conference area, or someone on a call will raise their voice, and suddenly I’m right back in it for a few seconds. I get hit with the sounds and images from that night so strongly that I lose track of what I was saying.
Are there specific people, places, or things that you avoid because they remind you of that night?

Yes. I take the long way around the building so I don’t have to pass near that area. I avoid that floor whenever I can. And if people start talking about the contractor or the cutover, I usually just shut the conversation down or get out of it.
Do you ever have flashbacks to that night when you're not expecting them, like when you're falling asleep or waking up?

Yes, it can happen when I’m not expecting it. It’s more when I’m in that conference area or if someone raises their voice on a call, but it just sort of hits me — the images and sounds from that night — and for a moment I lose track of what I was saying.
Have you been having trouble sleeping lately?

Yes. Most nights I have trouble falling asleep because I’m lying there replaying parts of what happened at the office. And then when I finally do fall asleep, I’ll wake up tense from a dream or even just some little noise. I feel worn out before the workday even starts.
Have your symptoms or behaviors been causing problems for you at work or in your personal relationships?

Yes. At work, it’s become a real problem. My last performance review was the first time I was told I’m missing key handoffs, leaving meetings abruptly, and that the team has to work around me.

And at home… my husband says it feels like I’m barely present anymore. I don’t like hearing that, but I know what he means.
Do you try to avoid thinking about what happened that night?

Yes. I try not to think about it. I’ll take the long way around the building just so I don’t have to pass that area, and I avoid that floor when I can.

If people start talking about the contractor or the cutover, I kind of shut the conversation down or find a reason to leave. I know I’m doing it, but I just don’t want to go back there in my head.
Do you often feel on edge or have difficulty calming down after you've become upset or anxious?

Yes. I feel jumpy a lot of the time. If a door slams, or someone comes up behind my chair, or my phone rings suddenly, I jerk like something bad just happened. My hands will shake, and it takes me a few minutes to calm down and look normal again.
How long have you been experiencing these symptoms?
It started after that late-night cutover incident. So… a little over a year now, about 13 months.
Do you avoid certain people because they remind you of that night?

Yes, I do. Mostly anyone tied to that contractor or the cutover. If people start talking about them, I shut the conversation down or leave. And I’ll take the long way around the building or avoid that floor so I don’t run into reminders of it.
Do you experience physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or trembling when you feel anxious?

Yes. The big one is trembling. If a door slams, or someone comes up behind my chair, or my phone rings out of nowhere, I jerk hard and my hands start shaking. It takes me several minutes to settle down and look normal again.
Do you often find yourself constantly on the lookout for potential dangers or threats?
I’m not sure. I don’t think of it as looking for danger exactly. I do notice I stay more aware of who’s around me, especially in certain places, but I’m not sure how constant it is.
Do you often feel like you're constantly on the lookout for something that might go wrong?

I don’t know if I’d say constantly. I haven’t really thought of it that way. I do catch myself checking what’s going on around me sometimes, but I’m not sure it’s all the time or exactly about something going wrong.
Do you often feel like you're waiting for something bad to happen?

Yes… I think so. Even when nothing is happening, there’s this fear sitting in my chest, like I can’t fully relax. And I feel ashamed too, like I should have handled things better somehow. It’s like if I let my guard down, something could still happen.
